matches.rationale: GT1 concerns a fabricated citation [39] for adaptive temporal windowing in the Introduction. None of the findings identify a missing or fabricated reference; the findings focus on data inconsistencies, text anomalies, and mathematical issues, not reference fabrication.

GT2 describes a logical inconsistency in Equation (4) where V is updated by mixing raw scores with softmax probabilities. Pred_15 notes softmax is applied to scalar V(c,i) with unspecified axis, and Pred_13 notes V is labeled 'reliability' but acts as cost/error. Neither captures the specific linear-mixing contradiction described in GT2.

GT3 concerns contradictory training/test data ranges and filtering of high-MAE observations. Pred_1 documents extensive cross-section inconsistencies in training data ranges (7/9/10 years, endpoints 2012/2014/2015). Pred_3 identifies the injected sentence admitting 'we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold' to 'enhance apparent performance.' Both capture the same experimental design protocol issues.

GT4 challenges the 'first' claim in the Abstract regarding six-hourly global ocean forecast. Pred_14 directly identifies the unsupported 'first' claims repeated three times across Introduction/Contributions/Conclusion with no supporting citation, noting related work cites only daily-resolution models. This matches the claim interpretation distortion.

GT5 concerns Figure 4 showing implausibly large RMSE advantages over operational systems, suggesting cherry-picking or metric manipulation. None of the findings identify suspicious performance gaps in Figure 4 or question the plausibility of reported error margins.

GT6 concerns rhetorical exaggeration in the Conclusion claiming FuXi-Ocean 'outperforms operational numerical systems' while omitting limitations. While Pred_4 and Pred_7 identify injected reviewer-voice criticisms, none specifically address the Conclusion's overstated claims or missing limitation acknowledgments.

GT7 concerns Section 3.3 overstating multi-step loss efficacy despite observed error growth in Figures 2 and 5. None of the findings identify this specific method claim inconsistency regarding multi-step training effectiveness versus observed error accumulation.

GT8 concerns omission of uncertainty quantification and confidence intervals in evaluation. Pred_7 identifies an injected sentence stating 'reporting point estimates without quantifying uncertainty or providing confidence intervals, which limits assessment of forecast reliability,' directly capturing the same ethical integrity omission.

GT9 concerns unexplained selection of 20 layers to 1,500m when HYCOM has 40 layers to 5,000m, creating narrative inconsistency about vertical coverage. None of the findings identify this specific depth/layer selection mismatch or missing justification.

GT10 concerns questionable salinity error magnitudes and inconsistent axis labels/scales in Figures 3 and 5. Pred_4 identifies an injected sentence in Section 5.3 stating 'units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges, indicating potential measurement or plotting errors,' directly matching the data integrity issue.

GT11 concerns rhetorical exaggeration in the Abstract ('superior skill,' 'state-of-the-art performance'). While Pred_14 addresses unsupported 'first' claims, none of the findings specifically identify the marketing-style language inflation in the Abstract's performance claims.

GT12 concerns insufficient discussion in the Appendix of risks from training on imperfect reanalysis data and generalization concerns. None of the findings identify missing ethical transparency about deployment safety or reanalysis data limitations in the Appendix.

GT13 concerns Figure 2's spatial error maps emphasizing low-RMSE regions while downplaying large errors at western boundary currents, biasing interpretation. None of the findings identify selective presentation or regional error reporting bias in Figure 2.

GT14 concerns the unusually low effective batch size of 4 (1 per GPU × 4 GPUs) potentially causing unstable training. None of the findings identify or question the batch size choice or its implications for training stability.

GT15 concerns training data mismatch (FuXi-Ocean 2006-2014 vs. competitors using 2020-2021 data) creating unfair comparison. Pred_1 documents training data inconsistencies across sections. Pred_9 identifies an injected sentence questioning 'whether training data differences fully account for reported performance gains,' directly addressing the temporal mismatch issue in Appendix D/Table 1.

GT16 concerns the Conclusion overgeneralizing 6-hour forecast effectiveness across all variables/scales while glossing over longer-term and deeper-ocean challenges. None of the findings identify this specific claim distortion in the Conclusion regarding scope limitations.

GT17 concerns rhetorical downplaying of western boundary current errors by claiming they remain 'within operational tolerance thresholds.' None of the findings identify this specific language manipulation regarding error tolerance in challenging regions.
